title: Mechatronic redesign of mechanical brushing apparatus to evaluate abrasive wear of road construction materials
author: Marín-Pareja, Rodríguez, et al.
materials: The wear test methodology follows AASHTO T135 [6] and ASTM D559 [7] and it incorporates the model used by the Tanzania Bureau Standards [13] Furthermore, the methodology includes the use of alternative wear systems instead of the brush specified in the standard. The samples were weighed, clamped to the wear equipment with a load of 13 N (3 lbf), and then subjected to 60 revolutions. At the end of the test, the samples were weighed again, and the mass loss was determined as a percentage of the original mass. Several tests were conducted to assess the ability and strength of each wear system to impart abrasion to a material, and the results were compared with those obtained using the original brush. steps.title: Characterize soil and prepare specimens
steps.instruction: Record soil properties (USCS classification CL, plasticity index 21 %, maximum dry density 1.626 g/cm³, optimum moisture content 22 %, sulfate content 0.48 mg SO₄/g, pH 5.2 at 22 °C). Cut natural soil into cylindrical specimens 5 cm (50 mm) diameter and 10 cm (100 mm) height, compact each to achieve the maximum dry density at the optimum moisture content, and weigh each specimen (initial mass).

steps.title: Assemble wear system and clamping mechanism
steps.instruction: Select one of the three interchangeable wear elements – serrated metal sheet (PLA), metal brushes (PLA), or commercial sandpaper (acrylic) – and mount it in the acrylic frame (84 × 59 × 65 mm). Install the linear bearing prototype (LM8UU tubular bearing with A380 aluminum housing) to replace the original channel/slot system, ensuring the displacement mechanism provides a constant, homogeneous load. Attach fastening rings to the specimen to fix and centre it on the rotation axis. Apply a fixed load of 13 N (3 lbf) in the upper quadrant of the linear bearing system. Enclose the entire assembly in the IP5X dust‑protection chamber (IEC 60,529) with a collection tray, confirming the enclosure material is acrylic.

steps.title: Connect power and electronics
steps.instruction: Plug the control box into a 110–120 V AC outlet (mains draw ≈0.01 A). The internal regulator supplies 5 V DC at 0.2 A to the sensors. Verify that the ESP32‑WROOM‑32S microcontroller, OLED display, optocoupler, mechanical relay, infrared sensor (5 V pulse width) and rotary encoder are correctly installed on the PCB (fabricated on a Bungard pro3000 CNC mill). Ensure the motor power rating can handle up to 10 A current.

steps.title: Configure test parameters on control panel
steps.instruction: Turn on the system with the black power switch. On the 1.3ʺ OLED screen, navigate the “DegasteU” menu using the rotary encoder: select option 1 “Laps” to stop by rotations or option 2 “Time” to stop by duration. Input the desired number of rotations (e.g., 60) or test time (minutes), confirm with the selector, and press the green start button. Set the motor speed to 60 rpm (if adjustable) and confirm ambient temperature is within 20–25 °C.

substeps.instruction: Press selector to open main menu.
Enter numeric value with selector and confirm (OK).
Press green button to start test.

steps.title: Execute wear test cycle
steps.instruction: Start the motor; the specimen rotates at 60 rpm while the 13 N load remains constant. The ESP32 monitors the infrared sensor and rotary encoder, counting rotations and elapsed time. The system automatically opens the relay to cut power when the programmed rotation count or time is reached. Observe rotation count and elapsed time on the OLED display. For validation, repeat the start‑stop sequence ten times to verify reliable automatic stopping.

steps.title: Post‑test weighing and data recording
steps.instruction: After the motor stops, open the dust chamber, remove the specimen, gently clean any adhered particles, and weigh it again. Calculate mass loss as a percentage: (initial mass − final mass) / initial mass × 100 %. Record the rotation count, test duration, and mass‑loss percentage for the cycle.

steps.title: Repeat for additional cycles or wear elements
steps.instruction: If multiple cycles are required (e.g., four cycles of 60 revolutions each), reinstall the same or a different wear element, re‑attach a fresh specimen, and repeat steps 4–6 for each cycle. Ensure the load, speed, and environmental conditions remain unchanged for comparability.
